messages:
anya: Thinking out loud — can we get a small exploratory panel that simulates per-invocation cost attribution for multi-model chains? Specifically to show how token-level cache savings and cross-model prefix reuse affect tenant chargebacks.

kevin: yes — been wanting this. do you mean a simulator where you can toggle 'cache hit rate' + 'model routing' and see per-model/unit cost change? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anya: exactly. minimal UI: select a chain (e.g. embed->reranker->gen), set sequence lengths & freq, set cache hit%, choose model SKUs (quantized vs fp16), then it outputs an amortized token cost table + waterfall.

jess: key UX thing: make cache credits explicit. tenants need to see "cache saved X tokens => credit Y" vs raw token burn. otherwise billing confuses them. also we should surface when savings are being applied to which model (first hop vs downstream).

samir: from infra side we can estimate per-token GPU cost easily, but attribution for chained requests is tricky when we have prefix-KV reuse. proposal: split cost into three buckets: compute (per-model token compute cost), kv-cache (prefetch/persist costs), and routing overhead (small). then attribute kv-cache savings back proportionally to downstream invocations that used it.

marta: design question: do we show "effective model unit cost" (cost/token after cache) or keep raw model cost + cache-credit line? I'm leaning raw + explicit credit so we don't mask spikes.

kevin: agree with marta. also add a slider for sample rate — cost panels will be noisy at 100% data, so let folks preview sampled economics.

anya: sketch of the attribution rule I tried in a quick notebook:

```
# pseudo
per_model_cost = tokens * unit_cost_sku
kv_credit = min(prefetched_tokens, used_tokens) * kv_unit_credit
attributed_cost = per_model_cost - (kv_credit * (used_tokens / total_used_tokens_for_chain))
```

kevin: hmm that looks reasonable but watch out for double-credit when prefetch happens on upstream model and downstream also does partial generation. maybe we need lineage tags: each cached prefix stores origin model id + origin invocation id. attribution only to chain invocations referencing that origin id.

jess: UI note: show two views — an "explain" view with a timeline for one invocation (token flow + credits) and an aggregated view (per-tenant per-day). Helps both debugging and chargeback.

samir: operationally we can reconstruct lineage for a sample of requests; full lineage for 100% would be heavy. so default aggregated view uses heuristics, and the explain view pulls full trace via sample_id.

anya: good. thought: include a "what-if routing" toggle to simulate fallback to cheaper model during burst — shows delta in latency + cost + quality (quality as a placeholder metric).

marta: small ask: surface whether credits are refundable when a downstream fails (e.g., rollback). accountants will ask. maybe show an "at-risk credits" line.

cost-bot: FYI — recent cost spike (1725498000) was 18% routing to fp16-gen, likely due to misrouting. link: https://console.redwood/cost/incidents/1725498000

kevin: thanks @cost-bot. That incident is exactly why this simulator would have been helpful. Can we add a "replay incident" import so PMs can load historical windows into the simulator?

anya: love that. next steps: I'll mock a data contract for the panel (sampled traces + per-sku unit costs + cache-meta) and post here. can folks reply with any additional must-have fields?

jess: must-have: model_variant, seq_len_p50/p95, token_directionality (prefix vs suffix usage), and link to eval set (quality delta).

samir: must-have from infra: KV hit/miss counts, prefetch counts, origin_trace_id, and GPU-seconds per-invocation.

kevin: add feature flag to gate this behind internal-only for now. we can prep a short demo for AE.

anya: cool — will post the contract in ~2 hours. thanks all :rock_on:
__metadata_note: This Slack thread is a simulated internal discussion about building a metered visualization for multi-model chain cost attribution. Messages are in chronological order; no title field per agents.md. All fields are strings or list of strings.
